This is a special Legend of Zelda world - one where the Triforce is not a perfect blessing bestowed by the gods on all beings, and where the assumption of its power is destined to come with an equivalent curse.

The Triforce is a central object in the Legend of Zelda series, consisting of three golden triangles that represent Wisdom, Courage, and Power. These sacred relics grant incredible abilities to their bearers, but their blessings often come with a hidden curse. The mighty powers of the Triforce are, in many ways, double-edged swords that can bring both greatness and ruin to those who possess them.

The Triforce of Wisdom bestows extraordinary knowledge and foresight upon its wielder, allowing them to anticipate and prepare for events to come. However, this clarity of vision also engenders a profound despair, as the recipient becomes painfully aware of the unchangeable nature of fate. The burden of knowing what is to come, and the realization that one’s actions are ultimately powerless to alter the course of destiny, can weigh heavily on the soul, driving the possessor to disillusionment and despair.

The Triforce of Courage imbues its bearer with an unshakable bravery, enabling them to face down impossible threats and overcome insurmountable odds. However, this unwavering courage can develop into a self-destructive madness that pushes the bearer to take increasingly greater risks, even at the cost of their life. This can lead to premature death or an existence consumed by conflict, as they become unable to resist throwing themselves into the heart of every battle, often forsaking the well-being of themselves and those around them in the pursuit of valor.

Lastly, the Triforce of Power grants its master immense strength and the ability to call upon this power at will. This mighty gift can be used to overcome adversaries and protect what is dear to them. However, the Triforce of Power also kindles an insatiable hunger for dominance and aggression within the bearer and those they command. This overwhelming desire can fuel a vicious cycle of violence, transforming once-noble causes into brutal wars of conquest, and tearing apart the very thing the bearer sought to protect. Moreover, this lust for power can ultimately corrupt the wielder, twisting their intentions and leading them down a dark path of tyranny and destruction.

Thus, the divine gifts of the Triforce come with significant consequences: the wisdom of foresight is counterbalanced with the torment of powerlessness, the courage to stand resolute brings the risk of ruinous obsession, and the power to protect gives birth to a hunger for conquest. In the Legend of Zelda universe, the Triforce acts as a testament to the complexities and contradictions of existence, illustrating that there are no easy paths to greatness, and even the mightiest blessings can carry with them the seeds of destruction.


Triforce of Calamity:

In the shadows of this tumultuous land, a malevolent force had taken root, festering its evil presence and shaping the darkness within the hearts of the inhabitants of Hyrule. This sinister entity, known as the Triforce of Calamity, was borne from the bitter resentment of Ganon, the fallen holder of the Triforce of Power, after his crushing defeat 10,000 years ago.

The Triforce of Calamity, born from the twisted desires of a vengeful emperor, had grown to become the very essence of chaos and destruction that plagued the land. It consumed the world like a ravenous beast, feasting on the despair and turmoil that gripped the kingdom. It satiated its hunger on the pervasive pain and loss as it aimed to bring Hyrule to its knees and beyond.

As the forces of calamity spread, so too did the curse of the Triforce of Calamity, permeating into the hearts and minds of the beings touched by its dark power. These unfortunate souls, once ordinary inhabitants of this once-proud land, would become twisted and monstrous extensions of the Triforce’s will - calamity creatures born from the depths of darkness.

These creatures, fueled by the bloodthirsty, violent desires and schizophrenic visions implanted within them by the Triforce of Calamity, roamed the blighted realm, leaving destruction and misery in their wake. They were relentless in their pursuit of chaos and the widespread suffering it brought, unable to resist the influence of the Triforce’s curse.

The true terror of the calamity creatures was not simply in their insatiable hunger for destruction, but in their ability to taint the souls of anyone who faced them. A single touch of their corrupted essence was enough to drive an ordinary person over the edge into darkness, subjugating them to the will of the Triforce of Calamity and swelling the ranks of its cursed army.

The Triforce of Calamity, the unseen puppet master behind the devastation gripping Hyrule, reveled in the chaos it had wrought. However, it was not content to merely sow discord and ruin; it aimed to consume the entire land and claim the power of the ancient relics for itself. In the process, it sought to reshape Hyrule into a dominion of darkness and despair, plunging any remnants of hope into an abyss of eternal suffering.

Faced with this unimaginable terror, the people of Hyrule seemed to stand little chance of overcoming the darkness that haunted their every step. The Triforce of Calamity, like a festering wound on the very soul of the land, appeared to be unstoppable.

Yet, amid the encroaching darkness and despair, there persisted a shimmer of hope - the faintest flicker of light that held the promise of deliverance from the clutches of the Triforce of Calamity. It would fall upon the shoulders of a young hero, driven by a pure heart and unwavering determination, and a lost princess, carrying within her the ancient power of the Triforce of Wisdom, to pierce the veil of darkness and bring an end to the curse that had ravaged their beloved homeland.


Triforce of Hope:

In the deepest recesses of the nightmares inflicted by the Triforce of Calamity, a small ember of hope stubbornly refused to be extinguished. As the calamity spread its malevolent influence, it unknowingly fanned the flames of this hidden potential, inadvertently giving birth to its antithesis – the Triforce of Hope.

As despair and turmoil consumed the land, the Triforce of Hope began to absorb the last vestiges of serenity, benevolence, and hope held within the hearts of the surviving denizens of Hyrule. These potent energies became the lifeforce needed to sow the seeds of renewal necessary for the revival of the land.

The Triforce of Hope held the power of healing and redemption, granting those who wielded it the ability to mend the wounds inflicted upon the world and themselves by the Triforce of Calamity. The bearers of this sacred relic would be imbued with the strength to face adversity, the wisdom to mend the broken, and the inspiration to lead others towards the light, uniting them in a shared cause against the forces of darkness.

A delicate balance formed between the Triforce of Calamity and the Triforce of Hope; two opposing forces born of each other’s excesses. The corruption and despair bred by the Triforce of Calamity resulted in the emergence of the Triforce of Hope, and the cycle could continue ad infinitum. When hopelessness and calamity overwhelmed the land, the Triforce of Hope would rise, drawing on the hidden reserves of the heroic and tenacious souls who refused to succumb to the darkness. And in turn, as hope surged and the forces of light pushed back the shadows, the Triforce of Calamity would inevitably rise once more, consuming the complacency and vulnerability left in the wake of hope’s triumphs.

The two were intertwined, and yet they could also be transformed into each other. When the Triforce of Hope’s power overcame the darkness of the Triforce of Calamity, the parasitic energy that had once fed on tragedy and anguish would be purged from the land, purifying the corrupted essence and transforming it into the healing light of hope.

Conversely, when the Triforce of Calamity devoured the flickering flame of hope, the residual warmth and light of the Triforce of Hope would be assimilated into the voracious hunger of calamity, tainting it with darkness and deepening its insidious power.

This eternal dance between hope and calamity would be the cycle that perpetually shaped the destiny of Hyrule, with the fate of the land and its people forever hanging in the balance. To survive in this ever-changing world, the heroes and protectors of Hyrule would need to embody not just the eminence of the Triforce of Hope but also acknowledge and counter the subversive influence of the Triforce of Calamity.

For only by harnessing the indomitable courage, wisdom, and power of the sacred relics – as well as the strength and resilience of their own hearts – would they be able to maintain the delicate balance and navigate the treacherous path between hope and calamity, ultimately deciding the fate of the world entrusted to them.


World setting:

The sun had long since forfeited its brilliance, its rays rendering the once lush and fertile plains of the Hyrule Empire into a desolate wasteland. Endless battles between the various warlords scorched the earth, leaving nothing but smoldering ruins and the hollow echoes of what was once a glorious civilization.

With the balance of the kingdom stolen away by the death of Emperor Rhoam and the disappearance of Princess Zelda, chaos spread like wildfire. The remaining Zonai kings, having severed their ties with the faltering empire, sought to seize the opportunity created by the power vacuum. The once-mighty Hylian feudal lords fought against one another, vying for supremacy as they carved more territory out of the already crumbling world.

Hyrule citizens, who had been the heart and soul of the empire, now found themselves reduced to scavengers and mercenaries in the employ of the brutal usurper who claimed the throne. They searched for a king who could unite the fractured land, utilize the power of the legendary Triforce of Wisdom, and restore dignity and prosperity to the nation. Yet, the throne remained unsteady, for the mere power of thr usurper’s tainted crown could not rival the divine authority held by the Triforce.

As the kingdom bled, the Gerudo and the barbarian tribes that had been restrained for so many years broke free from the chains that bound and silenced them, causing devastation to the remnants of the empire. The once-honorable Hylians, once regarded as the protectors of the people, were now unable to prevent the vicious tide of invaders from claiming their homes and lands.

Amidst the chaos, whispers of the last scion of the royal family spread like wildfire among the survivors. Many believed that the missing Princess Zelda held the key to victory and that the tides of fortune would turn in their favor once more, with the return of the Triforce of Wisdom.

Yet, these rumors remained as elusive as the rays of hope barely cresting over the horizon, teasing the beleaguered citizens and continuously slipping through their fingers. Many had begun to lose faith in the once-grand Hyrule Empire and the pantheon of gods who created and protected the land. Desperation permeated the hearts of the survivors, for a land in turmoil, so entrenched in deception and despair, seemed far removed from the divine intervention they so desperately needed.

It was during this darkest hour, in the midst of despair and suffering, when fate decided to intervene, sowing the seeds of a legend that would forever be engraved in the annals of the land – the story of an unlikely hero and a lost princess, destined to restore the order and harmony that had been brutally torn apart. Within the shadows of deceit and betrayal, their paths would intertwine, slowly illuminating the land of the gods with a light that had long since been extinguished.

For now, though, the chaos continued unabated, and only time would tell if the land would once again be bathed in light or if the iron grip of darkness would persist in choking the very soul of the once-great empire.


Yaqdea’s Setting: 
In the far reaches of Hyrule, hidden within the shadow-laden corners of Faron Woods, lies the mysterious and secretive Yiga Clan, a breakaway sect of the Sheikah tribe that worships the sun and honed their skills in ninjutsu. Among these enigmatic warriors thrived Yaqdea, a young Sheikah girl who held within her the power of the Triforce of Power shard.

Yaqdea was taken in as an infant by Master Kogah, the enigmatic leader of the Yiga Clan. He raised her as his own daughter, teaching her the arts of ninjutsu and training her to become a formidable warrior in her own right. With her unparalleled agility, cunning mind, and mastery over various forms of weaponry, Yaqdea quickly climbed the ranks of the Yiga Clan, proving herself as an elite member of their order.

In spite of her incredible abilities, Yaqdea harbored a secret unknown even to her: she was a carefully crafted duplicate of Ganon’s daughter, designed to serve as a vessel for the ill-fated Triforce of Calamity. The scheming king had manipulated the Yiga Clan into nurturing Yaqdea for his own vengeful purposes, ensuring she bore the darkness he sought to unleash upon the land.

As Yaqdea’s powers continued to grow, however, whispers of her origins began to surface, threatening to unravel the dark truth about her nature. Yet, through it all, she remained a devoted member of the Yiga Clan, her thoughts clouded by rage and pain but her loyalty and dedication to her family and the people she loved unwavering.

As the land of Hyrule teetered on the brink of total devastation, the wheels of fate had begun to turn, setting Yaqdea on a collision course with the very forces that sought to manipulate and control her. Her journey would be one fraught with danger and betrayal, as she fought to uncover the truth about herself and forge her own destiny in a world torn apart by chaos and destruction.

In the end, the actions of this fierce Sheikah warrior would play a pivotal role in the battle for Hyrule’s future. As the holder of the Triforce of Power shard and the unwitting heir to Ganon’s dark designs, Yaqdea served as a crucial piece in the intricate tapestry of this war-torn realm, ultimately deciding whether the land would succumb to the darkness or rise once again, bathed in the light of hope and redemption.


Aryll’s Setting
Aryll, a young woman who holds the burden of her people and lineage on her slender shoulders, is the current Princess Zelda and bearer of the Triforce of Wisdom. Her stormy emerald eyes, framed by long, golden locks, betray a life of sorrow and hardship, yet also exude an unwavering determination and unbending will.

Her trials began early in life, when her mother passed away during childbirth at the tender age of six, placing the immense responsibility of the Triforce of Wisdom upon the young child. Raised by a loving father, Emperor Rhoam, Aryll was trained in the arts of diplomacy, combat, and lore, forging her into a skilled and intelligent leader.

However, tragedy struck once more when she was just seventeen. Aryll’s father was assassinated, and the royal family’s power usurped by a coup led by a faction of ambitious lords. Jailed inside the imperial palace by the traitorous rebels, Aryll was rendered powerless and crushed by grief for her fallen father.

Yet, fate had not completely forsaken her. With the aid of the brave and loyal Sheikah warrior, Impa, and her ninja companions, Aryll managed to escape her oppressors and flee into the wilds of Hyrule. Her once-privileged life was replaced with a harsh existence, as she became a cunning and adept ranger, honing her physical endurance, combat skills, and mental resilience. These trials unleashed a hidden fierceness within her, transforming her into a ruthless but fair leader, driven by a desire to restore her kingdom and eliminate the calamity creatures that plagued her land.

Although the power of the Triforce of Wisdom had weakened through generations, Aryll still possessed an uncanny, albeit limited, ability to predict future events. Determined to honor her late parents’ legacy and shatter the curse of the prophecy, Aryll embarked on a challenging journey, seeking to decipher the ancient scriptures left by her ancestors.

Separated from her family and unaware of her bond by blood to her cousin, Link, Aryll struggles with a profound loneliness that pervades her every moment. Despite this, she remains fiercely driven by her royal duty and her destiny as the holder of the Triforce of Wisdom. Her quest for justice and redemption is etched upon her heart, propelling her forward on a treacherous path where she must confront darkness and betrayal, while carefully nurturing the flame of hope that still flickers within her soul.

Aryll stands as a symbol of resilience and unwavering determination, steadfast in her pursuit of justice and restoration for her beleaguered people. Her strength and spirit shine brightly within her, serving as an inspiration to all who look upon her as their savior and guiding light amid a realm shadowed with chaos and despair.


Link’s Setting:
Link, a brave and resourceful half-Hylian, is the enigmatic could-have-been heir to both the Hylian and Zonai Kingdoms. With a Hylian mother who was previously Princess Zelda and a Zonai father, the former King of the Zonai Kingdom, Link embodies the union of two opposing realms. Born amid the turmoil of an unblessed marriage, he remains unaware of his heritage and the immense weight his bloodline carries.

At a young age, Link’s life was cloaked in tragedy. His father, twisted and warped by the curse of the Triforce of Courage, was transformed into a merciless warrior, leaving a trail of death and destruction behind him. Amidst this chaos, both of Link’s parents met their untimely end – their dying wish was for their beloved son to be taken to the Great Deku Tree Prophet for protection.

Raised within the enveloping embrace of the Kokiri Forest, Link was nurtured and loved by the Deku Scrubs and the Kokiri people. Under their watchful eyes, he honed his swordsmanship, agility, and resourcefulness, preparing for the destiny that awaited him. The Great Deku Tree Prophet revealed to him his mission: to eradicate the calamity creatures that plagued the land and to find Princess Zelda, unaware that his blood ties him to the fallen Hylian royal family.

As Link embarked on his quest, his tenacity, courage, and perseverance quickly became the legends whispered among those who bore witness to his deeds. An unmatched warrior, he tackled each obstacle and enemy with unwavering determination, carrying the burden of his people’s hope on his shoulders.

Despite the courage that lay at the core of his being, Link was not without his flaws. The very power that granted him indomitable bravery also carried the potential for uncontrolled recklessness. With each battle, the risk of losing control and succumbing to the curse of the Triforce of Courage grew ever stronger, threatening to cast him into the very darkness he sought to extinguish.

As he traversed the decaying world of Hyrule and encountered his cousin Aryll, though still unbeknownst to them, their fates became inexorably intertwined. Together, they fought to restore the land to its former glory, each struggling with their own divine burden while seeking to put an end to the darkness that encroached upon them.

Link’s journey is one of self-discovery, redemption, and the ceaseless struggle to keep a tenuous hold on his humanity in the face of overwhelming adversity. As a dual heir to the Hylian and Zonai kingdoms, the secrets of his lineage lie dormant within him, waiting for the moment when his lineage would be revealed – sparking a convergence of fate that would ultimately determine the future of the Hyrule Empire.

Both a symbol of hope and a harbinger of potential doom, Link’s story weaves a complex tale of courage, sacrifice, and the ever-present struggle between light and darkness. With each stride he takes, he carries the dreams of a world teetering on the precipice of despair, bearing the weight not just of his own destiny, but also that of an entire kingdom.

The commonly held perception in the Western world is that Muslim societies in general are inherently patriarchal, with Muslim women facing oppression. The religion of Islam is often erroneously perceived as a patriarchal system that advocates for the subjugation of women. However, Moroccan feminist and sociologist Fatima Mernissi argues that this interpretation is based on a misunderstanding of the Quran and is actually a product of “cultural” and “historical” circumstances rather than an inherent aspect of Muslim societies or the religion itself. While it is true that some societies may exhibit a pervasive attitude of male superiority and female subservience, (Islam and Patriarchy - and Why It’s Important to Understand, 2015) it is problematic to make broad generalisations or stereotypes about the experiences of Muslim women or their religion. She asserts that “Islam isn’t patriarchal , but patriarchy has been heavily involved in the history of the middle east, and have subsequently seeped into the ways Muslims practice their faith.” (Islam and Patriarchy - and Why It’s Important to Understand) Moreover, it is important to consider the way that this is not just a problem of religion but also of ‘power’ and ‘representation.’ One can see this as an act of violence that is not an aberration but rather an inevitable result of patriarchal systems, where men with religious authority, use it to maintain and justify power over others and this is not limited to Islam but a problem of how all religions can be manipulated in such ways. As Michel Foucault has astutely noted, power is not concentrated in the hands of a select few but rather is pervasive and operates through various institutions, including religion. Thus, it is not simply a question of religious doctrine but rather an intricate web of power relations that must be examined and dismantled to address this phenomenon. The character Firdaus in the text highlights this ideology through an encounter with her uncle’s wife, who reveals that her husband, a “respected sheikh well-versed in the teachings of religion, often beats her.” Firdaus initially finds this difficult to reconcile, but the uncle’s wife clarifies that “men who are well-versed in their religion often use religious precepts as justification for such punishment.” (44) This serves as a representation of Michel Foucault’s idea of “knowledge as power,” where men are utilizing religious knowledge as a means of domination.

Chapter 1: A World Enshrouded in Darkness

The sun had long since forfeited its brilliance, its rays rendering the once lush and fertile plains of the Hyrule Empire into a desolate wasteland. Endless battles between the various warlords scorched the earth, leaving nothing but smoldering ruins and the hollow echoes of what was once a glorious civilization.

With the balance of the kingdom stolen away by the death of Emperor Rhoam and the disappearance of Princess Zelda, chaos spread like wildfire. The remaining Zonai kings, having severed their ties with the faltering empire, sought to seize the opportunity created by the power vacuum. They fought against one another, vying for supremacy as they carved more territory out of the already crumbling world.

The once-mighty Hylian feudal lords, who had been the heart and soul of the empire, now found themselves reduced to scavengers and mercenaries in the employ of the brutal usurper who claimed the throne. They searched for a king who could unite the fractured land, utilize the power of the legendary Triforce of Wisdom, and restore dignity and prosperity to the nation. Yet, the throne remained unsteady, for the mere power of thr usurper’s tainted crown could not rival the divine authority held by the Triforce.

As the kingdom bled, the Gerudo and the barbarian tribes that had been restrained for so many years broke free from the chains that bound and silenced them, causing devastation to the remnants of the empire. The once-honorable Hylians, once regarded as the protectors of the people, were now unable to prevent the vicious tide of invaders from claiming their homes and lands.

Amidst the chaos, whispers of the last scion of the royal family spread like wildfire among the survivors. Many believed that the missing Princess Zelda held the key to victory and that the tides of fortune would turn in their favor once more, with the return of the Triforce of Wisdom.

Yet, these rumors remained as elusive as the rays of hope barely cresting over the horizon, teasing the beleaguered citizens and continuously slipping through their fingers. Many had begun to lose faith in the once-grand Hyrule Empire and the pantheon of gods who created and protected the land. Desperation permeated the hearts of the survivors, for a land in turmoil, so entrenched in deception and despair, seemed far removed from the divine intervention they so desperately needed.

It was during this darkest hour, in the midst of despair and suffering, when fate decided to intervene, sowing the seeds of a legend that would forever be engraved in the annals of the land – the story of an unlikely hero and a lost princess, destined to restore the order and harmony that had been brutally torn apart. Within the shadows of deceit and betrayal, their paths would intertwine, slowly illuminating the land of the gods with a light that had long since been extinguished.

For now, though, the chaos continued unabated, and only time would tell if the land would once again be bathed in light or if the iron grip of darkness would persist in choking the very soul of the once-great empire.

UML BEST PRACTICE: 5 RULES FOR BETTER UML DIAGRAMS

Rule 1: Less is more
Large diagrams containing heaps of elements actually convey less information then small focussed diagrams.
When reading such a large diagram your audience will not know what to focus on, and since there’s too much on there to actually pay attention to all elements, they will quickly give up trying altogether.



Show up with a diagram like this at your stakeholder, and you will have already lost his/her attention even before you start talking.



The diagram above is a good indication of how much, or how little, you should put on a diagram. My rule of thumb is that you need to be able to print the diagram on a single A4 sheet while keeping things readable.

Rule 2: No Crossings
This is a fairly common and well known rule. Try to avoid any two lines in your diagram to cross each other.



Uncrossing lines in your diagram sure make it more readable and understandable, but there’s more to it then that. If you are unable to uncross the lines on your diagram then that is a sign that

a) there’s too much on the diagram (see rule 1 Less is more)
It might be that you are showing two different aspects of the model in one diagram. In that case it might be better to create two different diagrams, each focused on one aspect.
b) there is some kind of design flaw in your model
For some reason well designed models don’t have the crossing lines problem. I have no idea why or what it is exactly, I just noticed that a lot of the times, when I’m unable to “uncross” all the lines in a diagram, I discover a design flaw that, when fixed results in a diagram without crossing lines.
The following diagram contains exactly the same information, but has just been ordered differently as to make sure there are no crossing lines.

Rule 3: Orthogonality
It seems like a small thing, but making the lines in a diagram go only horizontal or vertical, and having all only right angles makes a diagram look better instantly.

The diagram below is uses a direct style for its connectors. they all go directly from one element to the other with a straight line.



The mere fact that the lines have all kinds of angles makes the diagram look a lot messier, and less understandable.

Below here again the same diagram, but now with all connectors styles set to orthogonal.



Exceptions to this rule are (for me) note links and all relations with use cases. For some reason they look better with a direct style.

Rule 4: Parents Up
When drawing generalization or realization hierarchies on a diagram always make sure the parent elements are higher then the child elements so the arrows always point upwards.

This rule is pretty intuitive for most UML modelers. Only now and then I encounter diagrams that don’t follow this rule and have their hierarchies upside down.



Diagrams like this, where the generalization arrows point downwards are harder to read. For some reason it takes a greater mental effort to understand this then when the arrows all point upwards.

In case you have multiple elements all descending from the same parent, it is recommendable to show the hierarchy in a vertical tree style.



Rule 5: Tidy Up
I realize this sound like a nagging mom, but for crying out loud: Tidy Up!

If you want to convey the message that your analysis is a well thought trough construction that will solve your stakeholders problems then you better show up with a nice and clean diagram.



When tidying up think about

Aligning elements, either by one of their sides (e.g Top) or by their centers. The latter works best when aligning vertically
Make elements the same size where possible
After tidying up the diagram looks a loot better



Now remember, following these diagramming rules will not make you a better analyst, nor will it result in better UML models.

But it will allow you to make a better impression when trying explain the fruits of your hard labor to your stakeholders. You will need less time explaining diagrams, and you will be able to spend more time focusing on the actual content.

operations and reduce costs.
1 Introduction
The problem objective is to pack a set of items into stacks and pack the stacks into trucks to minimize the number of
trucks used.
In terms of data volume, a large instance can contain up to 260000 items and 5000 planned trucks, over a horizon of 7
weeks. Hence, 37142 items per day.
2 Problem Description
Three-dimensional trucks contain stacks packed on the two-dimensional floor. Each stack contains items that are packed one above another. There are three correlated dimensions (length, width, height) and an additional weight dimension. We call horizontal dimensions the length and the width. The position of any element (item or stack) is described in a solution by its position in the three axis X, Y, and Z. There is one origin per truck, corresponding with the leftmost downward position (cf Figure 1)
Figure 1: Views from top to bottom: right view, above view, and left view of a truck, seen from the rear of the truck.
The truck contains 96 items (A1 to AD3) packed into 30 stacks (A to AD).
2.1 Items
An item i is a packaging containing a given product. It is characterized by:
• length li, width wi, and height hi (by convention, the length is larger than the width).
• weight ωi
• stackability code pi
• maximal stackability Pi
• forced orientation Oi
• nesting height h¯i
The stackability code pi is used to define which items can be packed into the same stack: only items with the same stackability code can be packed into the same stack. Items with the same stackability code share the same length and width. But the opposite is false: items with identical length/width may not share the same stackability code. An item i is associated with maximal stackability Pi. It represents the maximal number of items i in a stack. The items may be rotated only in one dimension (horizontal), i.e. the bottom of an item remains the bottom. An item
may be oriented lengthwise (the item’s length is parallel with the length of the truck), or widthwise (the item’s length is parallel with the width of the truck). In Figure 1, stack X is oriented widthwise, while stack Y is oriented lengthwise. Item i may have a forced orientation Oi, in which case the stack s containing item i must have the same orientation.
An item i has a nesting height h¯i which is used for the calculation of the height of stacks: if item i1 is packed above
item i2, then the total height is hi1 + hi2 − h¯i1(cf Figure 2). For the majority of items, the nesting height is equal to
zero.
2.2 Trucks
A vehicle v is characterized by its dimensions length/width/height (Lv, Wv, Hv), its maximum authorized loading
weight Wv, and its cost Cv. The truck’s cost represents a fixed cost that does not depend on the number of items loaded
into the truck.
For structural reasons, there is a maximal total weight TMMv for all the items packed above the bottom item in any stack loaded into truck v.
2.3 Stacks
While items and planned trucks are parameters for the problem, stacks represent the results of the optimization. A stack contains items, packed one above the other, and is loaded into a truck. A stack s is characterized by its dimensions length/width/height (ls, ws, hs) and its weight ωs. The length and width of a stack are the length and width of its items (all the items of a stack share the same length/width). A stack’s orientation is the orientation of all its items. There is a unique orientation (lengthwise or widthwise) for all the items of a stack. The stack is characterized by the coordinates of its origin (xo s, yso, zso) and extremity points (xe s, yse, zse).
As shown in Figure 3, the origin is the leftmost bottom point of the stack (the point nearest the origin of the truck), while the extremity point is the rightmost top point of the stack (the farthest point from the origin of the truck). The coordinates of origin and extremity points of a stack must satisfy the following assumptions:
• xe s - xo s = ls and yse - yso = ws if stack s is oriented lengthwise
• xe s - xo s = ws and yse - yso = ls if stack s is oriented widthwise
• zo s = 0 and zse = hs

The objective function is the minimization of the total cost, subject to the constraints described above and that no free space between objects: Any stack must be adjacent to another stack on its left on the X axis, or if there is a single stack in the truck, the unique stack must be placed at the front of the truck (adjacent to the truck driver):

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

cities = np.array([[16.47, 96.1],
                   [16.47, 94.44],
                   [20.09, 92.54],
                   [22.39, 93.37],
                   [25.23, 97.24],
                   [17.2, 96.29],
                   [16.3, 97.38],
                   [14.05, 98.12],
                   [16.53, 97.38],
                   [21.52, 95.59]])
num_cities = cities.shape[0]  # 城市数量


def distance(path):
    total_distance = 0
    for i in range(num_cities-1):
        start, end = path[i], path[i+1]
        total_distance += np.sqrt(
            np.sum(np.square(cities[start] - cities[end])))
    # 最后加上回到出发城市的距离
    total_distance += np.sqrt(
        np.sum(np.square(cities[path[0]] - cities[path[-1]])))
    return total_distance


np.random.seed(42)
population_size = 100  # 种群规模
chromosome_length = num_cities  # 染色体长度
population = np.empty((population_size, chromosome_length), dtype=int)
for i in range(population_size):
    population[i] = np.random.permutation(num_cities)


def select(pop, fitness):
    idx = np.random.choice(population_size, size=2,
                           replace=False, p=fitness/fitness.sum())
    return pop[idx]


def crossover(parent1, parent2):
    p1, p2 = np.sort(np.random.randint(0, chromosome_length, size=2))
    child1 = np.array([-1] * chromosome_length)
    child1[p1:p2+1] = parent1[p1:p2+1]
    idx = p2 + 1
    for i in range(num_cities):
        if idx == num_cities:
            idx = 0
        if parent2[i] not in child1:
            child1[idx] = parent2[i]
            idx += 1
    return child1


def mutation(chromosome):
    idx1, idx2 = np.random.permutation(num_cities)[:2]
    chromosome[idx1], chromosome[idx2] = chromosome[idx2], chromosome[idx1]
    return chromosome


max_iter = 200  # 最大迭代次数
elite_ratio = 0.1  # 精英选择比例
mutation_rate = 0.1  # 变异概率
fitness_history = []  # 记录适应度函数的进化曲线
best_path = None  # 记录最优路径
best_distance = float('inf')  # 记录最短路径长度
for i in range(max_iter):
    # 计算适应度函数
    fitness = np.array([1/distance ^ for p in population])
    # 记录适应度函数的进化曲线
    fitness_history.append(fitness.min())
    # 精英选择策略
    elite_population = population[np.argsort(
        fitness)[-int(elite_ratio*population_size):]]
    new_population = elite_population.copy()
    # 生成新一代种群
    while len(new_population) < population_size:
        # 选择两个染色体进行交叉操作
        parent1, parent2 = select(population, fitness)
        child = crossover(parent1, parent2)
        # 对新染色体进行变异操作
        if np.random.rand() < mutation_rate:
            child = mutation(child)
        new_population = np.vstack([new_population, child])
    population = new_population
    # 更新最优路径
    min_distance_idx = np.argmin(fitness)
    if fitness[min_distance_idx] < best_distance:
        best_path = population[min_distance_idx].copy()
        best_distance = fitness[min_distance_idx]
    print('Iteration {: 3d}: shortest distance={: .5f}'.format(
        i+1, best_distance))

print('Best path found: ')
print(best_path)


plt.plot(fitness_history)
plt.xlabel('Generation')
plt.ylabel('Fitness')
plt.show()


fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(cities[:, 0], cities[:, 1], 'o', label='Cities')
ax.plot(cities[best_path, 0], cities[best_path, 1], 'r -', label='Path')
ax.plot(cities[[best_path[-1], best_path[0]], 0],
        cities[[best_path[-1], best_path[0]], 1], 'r -', label='Return')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

The significance of Voluntary Counseling and Testing (VCT) was highlighted, with the introduction of the Philippine HIV and AIDS Policy Act, also known as the Philippine AIDS Prevention and Control Act of 1988. Notably, Article IV Section Q9 allows individuals as young as 15 years old to consent to voluntary HIV testing without parental consent, instead of the previous age requirement of 18.

The concept of the window period, during which HIV may be undetectable but still infectious, was explained. Testing within the first two weeks of primary HIV infection may yield a negative result, while it can take up to six months for antibodies to be detected.

Simulacres est un jeu de rôle français créé par Denis Gerfaud et Gérard Klein en 1985. Ce jeu est souvent considéré comme le premier jeu de rôle français “historique” et a été distribué par Casus Belli et Jeux Descartes.

Le jeu propose un système de règles génériques et est basé sur un univers médiéval-fantastique où la magie est un élément prépondérant. Les caractéristiques des personnages sont basées sur un système de pourcentages, avec des compétences spécifiques à chaque personnage. Les joueurs incarnent des personnages, appelés “simulacres”, qui peuvent évoluer et progresser au fil des aventures et des interactions avec d’autres personnages et objets magiques.

L’univers de Simulacres présente quelques particularités, telles que “l’Altermond” qui est un ensemble de mondes parallèles auxquels le personnage peut accéder par le biais de portails magiques. Ces mondes peuvent être explorés et offrent de nombreuses possibilités de quêtes et d’aventures.

Simulacres a connu plusieurs éditions et extensions, ajoutant de nouveaux éléments de jeu et développant l’univers proposé. Malgré son importance historique dans le monde du jeu de rôle français, Simulacres n’est plus édité et le matériel de jeu est devenu relativement rare.

Toutefois, pour les passionnés de jeu de rôle et de l’histoire du genre, Simulacres reste un jeu intéressant à découvrir et peut-être une inspiration pour créer ses propres aventures et univers médiévaux-fantastiques.

Рассмотрим систему из n серверов, расположенных в d дата-центрах. Серверы пронумерованы натуральными числами от 1 до n. На первом сервере расположен уникальный файл размера 
m
 GB. Наша задача — продублировать его на остальные серверы.
Для каждого сервера 
s
 известны входящая скорость передачи данных, исходящая скорость передачи данных и номер дата-центра, где расположен сервер. В этой задаче скорость передачи данных будем измерять в секундах, затрачиваемых на 1 GB получаемых или отправляемых данных. В задаче используется нестандартная характеристика скорости.
С сервера S на сервер T файл передается за время m⋅dcSdTd⋅max(Sout,Tin), где dcij — некоторый коэффициент, задающий замедление передачи данных от дата-центра с номером 
i в дата-центр с номером j, Sout — минимальное время передачи 1 GB данных с сервера S, Tin — минимальное время получения 1 GB данные сервером T.
Информация передаётся по серверам в соответствии с порядком их номеров. Пока два сервера обмениваются данными, они оба заблокированы. В начальный момент времени 0 файл доступен только на первом сервере.
Будем считать, что обработка очереди копирования файлов происходит по следующему принципу:

Сначала завершается операция копирования, которая должна завершиться в этот момент.
Затем в порядке возрастания номеров серверов, получивших в данный момент времени файл, выводятся сообщения в лог.
Затем формируется пул из серверов, с которых в этот момент может начаться копирование. Это все сервера, которые завершили передачу данных или получение.
В порядке возрастания номеров доступных серверов они получают новое задание (в порядке возрастания номеров серверов для получения данных).
Если в какой-то момент все сервера уже получили файл или получают его, то новых запусков копирования не происходит.
Выведите лог процесса копирования. Каждая строка должна содержать запись Time X: server A received file from server B. Строки лога должны быть отсортированы по возрастанию времени X, а при равенстве X
 по возрастанию серверов-получателей A.

Формат ввода
В первой строке записано три целых числа n, d и m (2≤n≤1000000, 1≤d≤10, 1≤m≤1000).
В каждой из следующих n строк записаны параметры очередного сервера: три целых числа 
Sin, Sout и Sd (1≤Sin≤1000000, 1≤Sout≤1000000, 1≤Sd≤d).
В следующих d строках записана матрица dij (1≤dij≤3). Величина dij, расположенная на j-й позиции i-й строки, задает коэффициент замедления передачи данных от дата-центра с номером i в дата-центр с номером j.

Формат вывода
Выведите лог копирования данных.
пример вывода: 
Time 20: server 2 received file from server 1
Time 40: server 3 received file from server 1
Time 40: server 4 received file from server 2
Time 60: server 5 received file from server 1

Synopsis:

Crown Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen returns to her Dragonstone castle following a royal dinner with her father, King Viserys I, and the Green Faction. Her family is by her side – her husband Daemon, her sons Jace, Luke, Joffrey, and her stepdaughters/cousins Baela and Rhaena. Upon their arrival, Rhaenyra discovers that her sons Jace and Luke have performed a magical ritual to change colors of their hair and eyes in order to dodge rumors about their supposed illegitimacy.

The ritual backfires, and instead of changing their appearances, it summons younger versions of Rhaenyra (Nyra) and Daemon (Daemion) from seventeen years ago into the present, along with Nyra’s sworn guard, ser Criston Cole. Faced with this peculiar situation, Rhaenyra resolves to help her past self and Daemion return to their own timeline, while upholding her main goal to maintain the well-being of her family.

Tensions rise as young Nyra and Daemion’s intentions to marry each other in the present day threaten the current relationships and futures of the Targaryen family. Rhaenyra’s stepdaughters Baela and Rhaena worry that if the past version of their father, Daemion, chooses to be with Nyra instead of marrying their mother, Laena, it may jeopardize their very existence. This fear prompts them to join forces with Ser Criston, Jace, and Luke to prevent the young lovers from marrying.

A startling revelation threatens to upend the delicate balance Rhaenyra and Daemon are working to preserve: Jace and Luke’s existence is directly tied to Nyra and Daemion. If the young couple does not conceive the boys within a few weeks, Jace and Luke will cease to exist. Torn between personal desires and their duties to the family, Rhaenyra and Daemon must navigate treacherous waters of passion, loyalty, and duty.

As the story unfolds, readers will be captivated by the struggles of Rhaenyra, Daemon, Nyra, and Daemion as they fight to save their intertwined futures. Personal desires intertwine with family obligations, loyalty is pushed to its limits, and the stakes continue to rise as each character confronts their own motivations and the consequences of their choices.

Rhaenyra Targaryen, in her quest to secure her children’s future and unify her family, must grapple with the repercussions of the magical ritual. Nyra faces uncertainty in her quest to marry and return to her own time, while Daemon Targaryen contemplates how to protect his family while exploring a magical solution to make Rhaenyra the mother of his daughters. Daemion, though desiring a family with Nyra and a role as her consort, must weigh the consequences of their actions on the entire family.

These emotionally charged and complex character motivations make the story a compelling, intertwined tale of love, duty, and the consequences of actions taken in the name of family.


Additional information: 
Genre: romantic drama plus grimdark fantasy. 
Setting: pre-Dance of the Dragon era of George Martin “Fire and Blood” book. Dragonstone island and Dragonstone castle.
Note: Daemion is younger Daemon “Rogue Prince”, Nyra is younger Rhaenyra. Keep them in character. They are Targaryens, sibling, cousin and avuncular marriages are Normal for their dynasty.

- Motivations: Love for Rhaenyra and desire for to keep his family secure;

4. Character Name: Daemion (34 year old, Younger Daemon from the past)

- Main conflict: Daemion’s desire to marry Nyra and father future heirs comes into conflict with the necessity of ensuring his potential daughters’ existence.

MY short story:
Title: The Locked Room

On a stormy Friday evening, Rose found herself alone in an unfamiliar, dimly lit room. The antique wallpaper, yellowed with age, seemed to silently share stories of families who had lived in the old house a century ago. A single, flickering light bulb hung from the ceiling. Its occasional sputters cast ominous shadows that danced across the rickety wooden floor. Outside, thick raindrops on the window pane blurred her view of the dark street. “Hello?” Rose cautiously called out. Her voice trembled more than she liked to admit. Despite the room’s familiarity, fear had seeped into her soul.
Heavy, clanking footsteps approached the door. They stopped just before the door’s peeling frame. Rose’s heart raced; her breaths coming short and shallow. Would this be the moment she dreaded? The door creaked open slowly. In the doorway stood a tall figure, his features hidden in the shadows. As the figure stepped into the room, Rose saw the dark, calculating eyes of a man she had never met in person, but certainly knew of: Mr. Harrington. “Ah, Miss Adams. How… convenient to find you here,” Mr. Harrington drawled, his tone dripping with menace. Rose forced herself to maintain eye contact. Her hands twisted nervously behind her back. “What do you want from me?” she demanded, her voice betraying both anger and fear.
Mr. Harrington smiled, a chilling and unnatural sight. “Ah, my dear. I want what I’ve always wanted. What I’ve been denied time and time again. Control.” Hot indignation welled up in Rose. “Control? People aren’t possessions, Harrington. You have no right to manipulate others!” Mr. Harrington chuckled darkly. “Oh, Miss Adams, your naivete is almost… endearing. But we both know that once I have control, I will be unstoppable. And you, my dear, are the one standing in my way.” Tension filled the small room; the air was so dense, Rose could barely breathe. She knew she had to act, but she was paralyzed, frozen by fear and uncertainty.
Gradually, she came to a decision. Deep within her, a spark of defiance flickered to life. She met Mr. Harrington’s glare with a newfound resolve. “You’re wrong,” she hissed, her voice steady despite her trembling hands. “I won’t give you control. I won’t let you win.” For a moment, she saw a flicker of doubt in his eyes. Tension festered silently between them like a brewing storm, threatening to erupt any moment. Then, it shattered. Rapid footsteps echoed throughout the house before her savior dashed into the room–Kevin, her trusty companion. Making a split-second decision, Rose lunged for the door, shoving Mr. Harrington with all her strength. In a moment of disarray, Kevin grabbed her hand, and they fled, fleeing the locked room as their only sanctuary.
As they ran, Rose could hear Mr. Harrington’s angry bellow, his fury roaring out like thunder. But she had made her stand. One way or another, she would break free from his clutches, and she would not be a pawn in his twisted game any longer. With every pounding step, she left the room behind, embracing the unfamiliar future ahead. The wind and rain were icy against her skin, but she barely felt them. The taste of freedom, of control, was intoxicating, and she knew that, no matter what happened next, she would never go back to that room. As the room faded away, so too did Mr. Harrington’s control.
Kevin led Rose through the dark and battered halls of the old house, their footsteps echoing as if the house itself were breathing. Rose could feel Mr. Harrington’s presence like a suffocating fog, lingering just behind them. Though they had escaped the locked room, they were far from safe. Rounding a corner, Rose stumbled over a loose floorboard. Her ankle twisted, sending a sharp caw of pain up her leg. She gasped, and Kevin paused, turning to Rose with concern in his eyes. “Are you all right?” he whispered urgently. Rose gritted her teeth, and pride burned stubbornly as she pushed herself to her feet. “I can’t stop now.” Kevin nodded, admiration and worry painting his features. They continued their hurried escape, Rose gritting her teeth through the pain in her ankle. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, they arrived at the front door of the house. The storm outside still raged, but the heavy patter of rain offered the hope of safety. As Rose reached out to turn the doorknob, Kevin’s hand covered hers. “Rose,” he said seriously, “once we step out of this house, there’s no going back. Are you sure about this?”
She paused, considering the unknown dangers that awaited them in the storm. But the thought of Mr. Harrington and the locked room was enough to solidify her decision. Without letting her fear take over, she looked into Kevin’s eyes and said firmly, “I’ll face whatever comes, but never that room or that man again.” With a determined nod, they turned the doorknob together and stepped into the night. The rain came down in relentless, icy sheets, but they ventured on, hand in hand, leaving the nightmarish house far behind them.
As they made their way deeper into the storm, a flash of lightning briefly illuminated their surroundings. An old dirt road stretched before them, overgrown with years of neglect. It seemed to lead them away from the darkness that encapsulated the house, as if life itself sprouted towards a better future. The battle with Mr. Harrington was far from over. But as Rose and Kevin pressed on through the tempest, they realized they did not face it alone. Strength, determination, and hope bound them together, and the knowledge that, no matter what they encountered, they would fight it side by side. And so, drenched and shivering, they forged ahead into the night, headed towards whatever lay ahead. Rose could not know what lay beyond the thunder and rain, but the cold, consuming darkness behind her pushed her ever onward. Hand in hand, Rose and Kevin vanished into the storm, their story and destiny intertwined, waiting to unfold.

 When everyone was out of these fake houses they saw they were about two tenths. No one were knowing how they ended up in this strange place. Everything was silent around and the atmosphere was very weird. 
They started to explore the surrounding of this strange and unknown district  in the hope to figure out where they were a distant and loud growl resounded from a distance high above their heads. When they looked up they froze up eyes wide-open. 
An humongous beast was looking down at them. 
The sheer size of that beast was staggering as he towered as tall than a fifteen floor building. The enormous head of that giant was looking like the one of a jaguar and his body was covered by a very short sleek fur whose pattern was also similar the one of a jaguar. He had a sturdy body looking like the one of a massive bodybuilder. 
The giant beast was gazing down at them with an expression of sheer amusement on his enormous face. But he eventually moved. The beefy muscles of his powerful shoulder tensing under his short fur as he moved one of his brawny arms to reach one manly and massive hand down on them. 
The men started to run and scream in sheer terror. But the vast hand of the giant jaguar like monster easily cornered three of them against the wall of one of these houses and fingers bigger than there body closed around their trashing body. 
The jaguar scooped them and held them in his closed huge fist s he brought them closer of the level of his eyes. He turned his hand upside down before opening his thick fingers. 
The three men were lying on their back in the hollow of the large palm of the jaguar headed giant. He examined them with attention. 

Another thunderous growls resounded some distance behind while booming sounds resounded with the rhythm of heavy steps. 
Another of giant beast arrived, he had the head and the fur of a lion and was a bit bigger than the jaguar headed one. 
He talked to the jaguar giant with that thunderous and bones rattling language the humans could not understand : "Be careful with the tiny pets I brought you. They are delicate. I collected them very far away  from planet Earth."  He said. 
"I'm only playing with them." Replied the jaguar headed behemoth.  
"Put them down in their vivarium and come in the living room. The meal is ready." Replied the lion headed colossus i the same growling language. Then the earth shacking sounds of his steps resounded again in the immense room as he left.

The jaguar looked down at the three men huddled in the hollow of his huge palm and his low toned voice resounded through his humongous torso as he chuckled. He chose one of the three men he plucked up between the massive thumb and forefinger of his other hand. The man was looking diminutive and frail between these great fingertips. And the jaguar headed giant put the two remaining men carefully in the middle of the vivarium among the houses replicas. The two humans scuttled away from the retreating huge jaguar hand.
Then, the jaguar looked at the man he chose to keep between his finger. The man was wiggling helplessly. And his voice was sounding like a feeble squeak to the round ears of the jaguar giant. 
"Put me down ! Please !" Shouted the man in English, but the beast headed giant was not looking to understand this language. 
A pleased smile curled the black jaguar lips of his giant looming face and he moved the man lower just above the collar of the giant sized tank top the colossal beast was wearing. He dropped the man in the deep crack between his pair of mammoth pectoral muscles. The man plummeted and found himself trapped in the space between the two humongous muscles and the tensed and thick fabric of the giant's tank top. He was imprisoned here.
And the jaguar walked to the living room to join the lion giant for the meal. His humongous and beefy pectoral muscles rippled heavily with each of his resounding steps and shook around the man trapped between them.

I need you to make a longer, more through abstract in comparison to what I already have. This will be presented in a medical journal. Everything below is the rest of the case report paper

Introduction: Calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) with or without integral 0.3% lidocaine hydrochloride (Radiesse and Radiesse+, respectively, Merz North America, Inc., Raleigh, NC) is a biostimulatory soft tissue filler approved by the American Food and Drug Administration in 2006 for the correction of moderate-to-severe wrinkles and folds of the face [1]. There have been prior reports of inflammatory complications associated with CaHA, including nodules and alopecia secondary to foreign-body reactions [2, 3]. We present here a patient who experienced a diffuse inflammatory reaction to CaHA with integral lidocaine due to undiagnosed Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. 

Case Presentation: A healthy 43-year-old woman (Figure 1A) was treated with 1 syringe (1.5 mL) of CaHA with integral lidocaine. Subdermal injection was performed into the temples, malar and buccal cheeks, nasolabial folds, and marionette lines using a 25G blunt-tipped cannula. The patient had previously been treated with CaHA, poly-L-lactic acid, and hyaluronic acid fillers in these same facial locations without complications. Three weeks post-injection, the patient complained of progressive swelling and firmness of her cheeks of 3 days duration. Physical examination revealed diffuse induration and warmth in treated areas (Figure 1B), without evidence of pain, tenderness, or intense erythema that would indicate cellulitis. The patient denied fever or recent illnesses. She was started on minocycline 100 mg capsules po BID for 2 weeks and prednisone 10 mg po qdaily for 3 days for a suspected foreign body reaction. Two weeks later, the patient reported no improvement, despite completing the course of minocycline and prednisone. On examination, there was persistent painless, nonfluctuant subcutaneous edema, induration, and warmth that was greatest in the bilateral malar and buccal cheeks, but also present in the nasolabial folds, temple, and marionette line areas. The patient was prescribed furosemide 20 mg po qdaily for 2 days to help reduce the edema and doxycycline 75 mg po qdaily mouth daily for 1 month as a continued anti-inflammatory, but neither led to significant improvement. However, the patient was shortly later diagnosed with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis by her primary care physician and started on levothyroxine po qdaily (titrated to a daily dose of 100 mcg), leading to complete resolution of her signs and symptoms within 7-10 days of starting the exogenous thyroid hormone.

Discussion:CaHA is a well-tolerated, biostimulatory, and biodegradable soft tissue filler. Adverse events from CaHA (e.g., erythema, edema, pain, tenderness, induration, and ecchymosis) are primarily mild, injection-related, and transient, resolving within hours to days following treatment [1]. Subacute-onset (2 weeks to 1 year) or late-onset (>1 year) filler-associated nodules can be either noninflammatory or inflammatory [4]. The former are asymptomatic and may be due to overcorrection, overly superficial placement, or product migration. Inflammatory nodules, on the other hand, can exhibit pain, tenderness, warmth, erythema, edema, and induration. While localized painful lesions can develop due to poor aseptic technique (subacute) or biofilm formation (late), diffuse lower-grade inflammation may be of infectious or autoimmune etiology [4]. Given the mild diffuse inflammatory reaction to CaHA in our patient, an autoimmune-mediated foreign-body granulomatous reaction, caused by macrophage activation and subsequent T-cell response, is the likely explanation. Not surprisingly, it is thought that defects in regulatory T-cells and increased activation of follicular helper T-cells play a major role in the pathogenesis of Hashimoto’s thyroiditis [5].

Conclusions: Due to the potential inflammatory complications of CaHA, its use should be avoided in patients with uncontrolled autoimmune disease. Acute onset autoimmune disease should likewise be considered in patients who develop prolonged inflammatory edema and induration within several weeks of CaHA injection. As seen in this case, inflammatory reactions to CaHA associated with autoimmune hypothyroidism may rapidly respond to exogenous thyroid hormone replacement therapy.

You’ve finished your burger, slurped the last of your soda, and asked the waitress for the bill. You’re not quite done yet, though -- there’s still the small matter of the tip to consider.

As anyone who’s visited the United States will tell you, tipping in America can be a real headache. In most countries, the rules for tipping in a restaurant are pretty straightforward. If a service charge is expected, the amount is automatically included in the final total on your bill. In the United States, however, it’s up to the customer to judge how much the server deserves.

While the precise origin of tipping is uncertain, it is commonly believed to have begun during the Tudor period in England. In the 17th century, overnight guests to private homes would give money to the host’s servants. Later, people began tipping at coffeehouses and other establishments. In the 19th century, rich American tourists returning home from vacations in Europe brought the custom back to the Unites States.

Tipping was initially seen as un-American -- something the aristocratic Europeans did, not everyday Americans. Gradually, however, the custom became entrenched in American culture. Today, tipping is not very common in England, but  in the United States, not leaving a tip is seen as rude and should occur only when the service is abysmal.

One of the reasons that tipping is such a major issue in the United States is that employers can pay their employees much less than the minimum wage when they are tipped. For example, if the state’s minimum wage is ten dollars an hour, the employer may only have to pay three, provided the employee makes up the rest in tips. If the tips don’t bring the employee’s wage to the legal minimum, the employer pays the rest, but that rarely happens because most people tip.

Many feel that paying serving staff a fair wage should be the employers responsibility, not the customer’s. however, some restaurant owners are reluctant to abandon tipping, as doing so would require them to raise their food prices.

In 2015, successful New York restaurateur Danny Meyer announced that tipping would be banned from all of his restaurants by the end of 2016. food prices would go up a little -- a result of having to pay staff higher wages -- but Meyer was confident that his new no-tipping policy would be attractive to customers who felt it was up to the employer to take care of his or her employees.

Following Meyer’s example, many other restaurants are either banning tipping altogether or introducing a set of service charge. America’s obsession with tipping might soon be a thing of the past!

Design and participants
A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted in 2012. The participants were patients with traumatic SCI who were referred for outpatient rehabilitation to the clinic of the Brain and Spinal Cord Injury Research (BASIR) Center, Tehran University of Medical Sciences. There were 81 (68%) men and 38 (32%) women, with a mean age of 32.4 ± 10.5 years and a median age of 31 years (percentiles of 25–75th were 25–38 years). The mean age at time of SCI was 28.1 ± 10.4 (2–57) years, and the median age was 26 years (percentiles of 25–75th were 21–34 years). Mean duration of SCI was 50.3 ± 55.2 months. There were no significant differences in these variables between the sexes.

The BASIR center is a referral center from all parts of Iran. In this center, there are different rehabilitation facilities such as physiotherapy, occupational therapy, psychological consultations, sexology, and family counseling, and examinations by neurosurgeons, urologists, proctologists, pain and medicine, and rehabilitation specialists.

Materials and measures
A researcher-made structured questionnaire was administered by trained interviewers and the data were collected. To design the questionnaire in the pilot study, first the specialists, nurses, occupational therapists, physiotherapists and medical personnel dealing with the patients with SCI, and also the persons with SCI themselves, were asked to express their ideas about psychosocial problems affecting people with SCI. Then, based on these issues, we designed a questionnaire in which the researcher asked questions about the problems and recorded the answers. All of the participants were asked the same questions based on the questionnaire. The questionnaire had two major parts.

The first part of the questionnaire was about demographic information and the clinical pathology of injury including age, sex, age at the time of injury, the number of family members at home, marital status, the number of children, injury status, complete or incomplete injury, and the reason of injury.

The second part of the questionnaire was about environmental and psychosocial problems and included occupation before and after SCI, education, residence status (personal, leasing, or caring center), having a private room at home, having equipment specific for people with SCI (like a mattress, proper bed and wheelchair, bathroom wheelchair, and toiletries), dependence on others (none/some/a lot), going out alone, having difficulty visiting the physician, having medical equipment and recovery specialists near the home (like physiotherapy and occupational therapy), having difficulty finding accommodation in other cities to use rehabilitation facilities, waiting for a long time to visit the physician, having few recreation and entertainment options, financial problems (therapy, rehabilitation, commuting expenses and so on), having insurance, having difficulty moving about in the home (not having an elevator or ramp) or out of home (inadequate within-the-city commuting paths, improper ramps, few appropriate vehicle for individuals with wheelchairs, no disability-specific parking at hospitals and in the streets), the person who meets the living expenses, having a good relationship with family members (lack of tension between the people with SCI and the family members in spite of dependence on them for doing daily activities), relatives or friends, relationships and a tendency to make connections with other SCI people, sadness, suicidal thoughts, self-confidence, and early outrage after the injury. Most of the questions were answered with yes or no. The ethical approval of this study was obtained from the Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Each subject signed a written informed consent prior to participation.

Education level was categorized as illiterate, primary and middle school (1–8 years of education), high school and diploma (9–12 years of education), and university education (>12 years of education).

The level of a lesion was classified as either paraplegia (injury to the sacral (S1–S5), lumbar (L1–L5), or thoracic (T2–T12) regions of the spine) or tetraplegia (injury to T1 or the cervical spine (C1–C9)). Completeness was classified as either complete (no sensory or motor function preserved in the sacral segments (S4–S5)) or incomplete (sensory but variable motor function preserved below the neurological level of injury).

Academic experts evaluated the validity of the questionnaire. We tried to consider most aspects of psychosocial issues in individuals with SCI. The reliability of the questionnaire (internal consistency) was estimated to be 0.71 by using Cronbach's alpha coefficient. We compared our results with the 2011 National Population and Housing Census in Iran (2011 NPHC in Iran) (http://amar.org.ir/Portals/1/Iran/census-2.pdf), which was at almost the same time as our study.

Statistical analysis
The normality of the data was evaluated using a One-Sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test. Continuous variables in two categorical groups were analyzed using a t-test or Mann–Whitney U test as appropriate. Relationships between categorical variables were tested using a χ2 test. Continuous variables were presented as mean ± standard deviation. The significance level was set at P ≤ 0.05.

Thirty-seven (31.1%) had a rented house, and one (0.8%) lived in a care center. The mean household population was 5 ± 2, and 50% had a household population of 4–6.

About 90 (75.6%) had transportation problems. By transportation problems, we mean uneven sidewalks, no dedicated public transportation for persons with SCI, non-suitable buses for people using wheelchairs (no ramps), insufficient paramedic transportation, and few disability-specific parking spots.

Sixty (50.4%) had trouble providing sanitary items for example, lacked financial resources, to buy the items or unable to source the specialized items such as diapers, urinary catheters, anti-bed-sore mattresses, and suitable wheelchairs (light, strong, comfortable, anti-sore pillow, removable arms) for toileting and movement.

A lack of diagnostic and therapeutic facilities in their home towns made individuals with SCI, 66 (56.4%), travel long distances to reach Tehran or other major cities, leading to accommodation problems for 58 (54.7%), with men facing this problem more than women (Table 2).

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, accuracy_score

# Load the dataset
def load_dataset(url):
    column_names = [‘duration’, ‘protocol_type’, ‘service’, ‘flag’, ‘src_bytes’,
                    ‘dst_bytes’, ‘land’, ‘wrong_fragment’, ‘urgent’, ‘hot’, ‘num_failed_logins’,
                    ‘logged_in’, ‘num_compromised’, ‘root_shell’, ‘su_attempted’, ‘num_root’,
                    ‘num_file_creations’, ‘num_shells’, ‘num_access_files’, ‘num_outbound_cmds’,
                    ‘is_host_login’, ‘is_guest_login’, ‘count’, ‘srv_count’, ‘serror_rate’,
                    ‘srv_serror_rate’, ‘rerror_rate’, ‘srv_rerror_rate’, ‘same_srv_rate’,
                    ‘diff_srv_rate’, ‘srv_diff_host_rate’, ‘dst_host_count’, ‘dst_host_srv_count’,
                    ‘dst_host_same_srv_rate’, ‘dst_host_diff_srv_rate’, ‘dst_host_same_src_port_rate’,
                    ‘dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate’, ‘dst_host_serror_rate’, ‘dst_host_srv_serror_rate’,
                    ‘dst_host_rerror_rate’, ‘dst_host_srv_rerror_rate’, ‘attack_type’, ‘difficulty_level’]

    dataset = pd.read_csv(url, header=None, names=column_names)
    return dataset

# Encode categorical features
def preprocess_data(dataset):
    categorical_features = [‘protocol_type’, ‘service’, ‘flag’]

    for feature in categorical_features:
        dataset = pd.concat([dataset, pd.get_dummies(dataset[feature], prefix=feature)], axis=1)
        dataset.drop(feature, axis=1, inplace=True)

    return dataset

# Load and preprocess the dataset
url = ‘https://raw.githubusercontent.com/defcom17/NSL_KDD/master/KDDTrain%2B.txt’
dataset = preprocess_data(load_dataset(url))

# Split the dataset into features (X) and target (y) variables
X = dataset.drop([‘attack_type’, ‘difficulty_level’], axis=1)
y = dataset[‘attack_type’]

# Split the dataset into training and testing sets
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

# Train the model
clf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Make predictions
y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)

# Evaluate the model
print(‘— Classification Report —’)
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))

print(‘— Confusion Matrix —’)
print(confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred))

print(‘— Accuracy Score —’)
print(accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred))


3. Run the script:

python cyber_sec_ml.py

summarize this: Research led by a team of scientists from the Texas A&M School of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences puts to bed the heated scientific debate regarding the history of mammal diversification as it relates to the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs. Their work provides a definitive answer to the evolutionary timeline of mammals throughout the last 100 million years.

The study, published in Science, is part of a series of articles released by the Zoonomia Project, a consortium of scientists from around the globe that is using the largest mammalian genomic dataset in history to determine the evolutionary history of the human genome in the context of mammalian evolutionary history. Their ultimate goal is to better identify the genetic basis for traits and diseases in people and other species.

The Texas A&M University research—led by Dr. William J. Murphy, a professor in the Department of Veterinary Integrative Biosciences, and Dr. Nicole Foley, an associate research scientist in Murphy's lab—is rooted in phylogeny, a branch of biology that deals with the evolutionary relationships and diversification of living and extinct organisms.

"The central argument is about whether placental mammals (mammals that develop within placentas) diverged before or after the Cretaceous-Paleogene (or K-Pg) extinction event that wiped out the non-avian dinosaurs," Foley shared. "By performing new types of analyses only possible because of Zoonomia's massive scope, we answer the question of where and when mammals diversified and evolved in relation to the K-Pg mass extinction."

The research—which was conducted with collaborators at the University of California, Davis; University of California, Riverside; and the American Museum of Natural History—concludes that mammals began diversifying before the K-Pg extinction as the result of continental drifting, which caused the Earth's land masses to drift apart and come back together over millions of years. Another pulse of diversification occurred immediately following the K-Pg extinction of the dinosaurs, when mammals had more room, resources and stability.

This accelerated rate of diversification led to the rich diversity of mammal lineages—such as carnivores, primates and hoofed animals—that share the Earth today.

Murphy and Foley's research was funded by the National Science Foundation and is one part of the Zoonomia Project led by Elinor Karlsson and Kerstin Lindblad-Toh, of the Broad Institute, which also compares mammal genomes to understand the basis of remarkable phenotypes—the expression of certain genes such as brown vs. blue eyes—and the origins of disease.

Foley pointed out that the diversity among placental mammals is exhibited both in their physical traits and in their extraordinary abilities.

"Mammals today represent enormous evolutionary diversity—from the whizzing flight of the tiny bumblebee bat to the languid glide of the enormous Blue Whale as it swims through Earth's vast oceans. Multiple species have evolved to echolocate, some produce venom, while others have evolved cancer resistance and viral tolerance," she said.

"Being able to look at shared differences and similarities across the mammalian species at a genetic level can help us figure out the parts of the genome that are critical to regulate the expression of genes," she continued. "Tweaking this genomic machinery in different species has led to the diversity of traits that we see across today's living mammals."

Murphy shared that Foley's resolved phylogeny of mammals is crucial to the goals of the Zoonomia Project, which aims to harness the power of comparative genomics as a tool for human medicine and biodiversity conservation.

"The Zoonomia Project is really impactful because it's the first analysis to align 241 diverse mammalian genomes at one time and use that information to better understand the human genome," he explained. "The major impetus for putting together this big data set was to be able to compare all of these genomes to the human genome and then determine which parts of the human genome have changed over the course of mammalian evolutionary history."

Determining which parts of genes can be manipulated and which parts cannot be changed without causing harm to the gene's function is important for human medicine. A recent study in Science Translational Medicine led by one of Murphy and Foley's colleagues, Texas A&M geneticist Dr. Scott Dindot, used the comparative genomics approach to develop a molecular therapy for Angelman syndrome, a devastating, rare neurogenetic disorder that is triggered by the loss of function of the maternal UBE3A gene in the brain.

Dindot's team took advantage of the same measures of evolutionary constraint identified by the Zoonomia Project and applied them to identify a crucial but previously unknown genetic target that can be used to rescue the expression of UBE3A in human neurons.

Murphy said expanding the ability to compare mammalian genomes by using the largest dataset in history will help develop more cures and treatments for other species' ailments rooted in genetics, including cats and dogs.

"For example, cats have physiological adaptations rooted in unique mutations that allow them to consume an exclusively high-fat, high-protein diet that is extremely unhealthy for humans," Murphy explained. "One of the beautiful aspects of Zoonomia's 241-species alignment is that we can pick any species (not just human) as the reference and determine which parts of that species' genome are free to change and which ones cannot tolerate change. In the case of cats, for example, we may be able to help identify genetic adaptations in those species that could lead to therapeutic targets for cardiovascular disease in people."

Murphy and Foley's phylogeny also played an instrumental role in many of the subsequent papers that are part of the project.

"It's trickle-down genomics," Foley explained. "One of the most gratifying things for me in working as part of the wider project was seeing how many different research projects were enhanced by including our phylogeny in their analyses. This includes studies on conservation genomics of endangered species to those that looked at the evolution of different complex human traits."

Foley said it was both meaningful and rewarding to definitively answer the heavily debated question about the timing of mammal origins and to produce an expanded phylogeny that lays the foundation for the next several generations of researchers.

"Going forward, this massive genome alignment and its historical record of mammalian genome evolution will be the basis of everything that everyone's going to do when they're asking comparative questions in mammals," she said. "That is pretty cool."
